article_title: Analysing AI utilisation in education through learner question types: A constructivist approach
citation: Lee, H., Atif, A., & Kang, K. (2026). Analysing AI utilisation in education through learner question types: A constructivist approach. Australasian Journal of Educational Technology, 42(1), 79–96. https://doi.org/10.14742/ajet.10657
title: Dataset of 434 expert-labelled authentic learner questions augmented to balance class distributions
description: A corpus of "434 authentic questions" collected from "11 students across 12 information technology courses", which were "expert labelled and augmented to balance class distributions". The dataset instantiates the constructivist three-role question taxonomy and serves as the training and evaluation data for the BERT, DeBERTa and RoBERTa classification models tested in the study.
requirements: Expert labelling of questions into the three role categories, plus augmentation to balance class distributions.
constraints: Data derive from 11 students across 12 information technology courses, a small single-discipline base the article itself flags via its call for cross-disciplinary validation.
target_learning_goals: classifying learner inquiry depth to support personalised feedback
examples: The corpus fed the evaluation in which DeBERTa reached the highest overall accuracy (86.36%).
